## PrototypeFramework — agent contract (synced)

This project consumes **`com.classicspins.prototype-framework`**. The framework's rules apply to
every change here. Full text: [`docs/framework/AGENTS.framework.md`](./docs/framework/AGENTS.framework.md).
Shape and placement: [`docs/framework/architecture-map.md`](./docs/framework/architecture-map.md).
Type → assembly → file lookup: `docs/framework/framework-api.index.json` (**use it instead of
grepping**). Task procedures: [`docs/framework/recipes/`](./docs/framework/recipes/).

Skills under `.claude/skills/pf-*` load the operational detail on demand: `pf-framework-rules`,
`pf-architecture`, `pf-add-screen`, `pf-add-dialog`, `pf-add-key`, `pf-add-boot-node`,
`pf-add-event`, `pf-add-service-module`, `pf-world-space`, `pf-visual-design`, `pf-gates`,
`pf-uigate`.

### The five things that get a change rejected

1. **Framework code edited from inside this repo.** `Library/PackageCache/…` is overwritten on every
   reimport (your edit is silently lost); editing an embedded copy forks the shared package. Fix it
   in the framework repo via dev-link instead — see `pf-gates`.
2. **A command-style event** (`ShowDialogEvent`, `PlaySfxEvent`). Events are past-tense facts; to
   make something happen, call that owner's service.
3. **A View that branches on game state.** A View answers *how it looks*; a controller answers *what
   happens*.
4. **A script no assembly claims.** No ancestor `.asmdef`/`.asmref` ⇒ it compiles into
   `Assembly-CSharp`, green and outside the AD-1 boundary. Doctor check 15 names it.
5. **A spine change made without routing it** — a new assembly beyond the SKU's eight, a reference
   edge, RenderLayer, kernel boot node, event type, or an edit to a shipped migrator is an
   architecture decision, not a patch.

### Where code goes: the assembly is the spine, the folder is the feature

Eight SKU assemblies mirror the framework's tiers name for name — `Game.{Domain, Application,
Presentation, Infrastructure, Composition, Views, Gen, Editor}` — each with an **anchor folder**
holding its `.asmdef`. A feature keeps its tiers together and joins each to its assembly with a
three-line `.asmref`; Unity picks the **nearest ancestor**, so the compiler enforces the architecture
while a review still reads one feature in one folder. **`namespace ≡ assembly name`.** Never
hand-create it — the Wizard emits the `.asmdef`s, `Scaffold.Sync` writes the `.asmref`. Two that
bite: **`Game.Presentation` names no container type** (ask Composition for a port), and **Domain /
Application / Gen are engine-free**, which is what lets the headless gate glob them. Detail:
`pf-architecture`.

### The 17 rules, one line each

1. Events are past-tense **facts**, never commands — to make something happen, call that owner's service.
2. **A shipped migrator is immutable** — append a new migrator + fixture, never edit one.
3. Never `string.Split(',')` on CSV — use the RFC 4180 parser.
4. No string literal reaches `SetText` from game code — all text goes through `LocKey`.
5. A boot node may only touch services its `Requires` capabilities assert are ready.
6. The framework never moves a node off-thread — CPU-heavy work self-hops via `UniTask.RunOnThreadPool`.
7. A new RenderLayer must pass the three-condition test; otherwise use `sortingOrder` in an existing layer.
8. Every View passes both review tests: the "why" test and the gallery test.
9. No input polling (`Input.GetTouch`, `OnMouse*`, `Touchscreen.current`) in `Game.Views` — EventSystem only; the sole exception is `IBackButtonRouter`. **CI grep.**
10. A controller never sees screen-space coordinates — the View converts to game units first.
11. A `[PoolLeak]` / "rented leak" WARN is **a bug to fix** (a missing `Return`), not noise. **CI grep.**
12. uGUI layout (incl. `TextProxy` stacks), particle tuning, bakes, mixer routing → **Unity-MCP**, never raw YAML.
13. New scene/dialog/widget → edit the manifest, run `Scaffold.Sync`. Never hand-create, never copy a template.
14. Models take `IRandom` by constructor — no `System.Random`, no `UnityEngine.Random`. Seed at the composition point and log it.
15. Real-time sim advances by a **fixed dt passed as a parameter**; no `Time.*` inside a Model; ticks flow through `GameplayTickDriver`; a pause gate decides whether the tick runs.
16. Parent is decided **per object**, never once per feature — ask *what does it anchor to* first: a screen edge (HUD, score, top bar) ⇒ uGUI under the `GetHost` of the layer that owns it (`Ui`, `Popup` for dialogs, `Overlay` for system overlays); the world ⇒ only then ask how it draws (`Renderer` ⇒ `WorldRoot`, `Canvas` ⇒ `GetHost(id)`).
17. A player-visible surface ships **visually finished, never a wireframe** — follow `docs/art-direction.md` if the artist wrote one; otherwise **you decide** the aesthetics and record them as design tokens. A placeholder needs an explicit human request.

The canonical wording of these rules is Vietnamese and is reproduced verbatim in
`docs/framework/AGENTS.framework.md` §1 — **when that text and this summary differ, the verbatim
rule wins.**

### Three-tier init law

> **Boot node ⟺ it must be _awaited_, OR it can _fail meaningfully_, OR it needs _external
> ordering_.** None of the three ⇒ plain DI construction (tier 1) or `IAsyncStartable` in the
> feature's own child scope (tier 3). A feature-init node in the kernel is a boundary violation.

### The rig ruler (world ⟷ canvas)

> **1 texture px == 1 canvas reference px == 1 world unit** — three links, all required: sprite
> import **PPU 1** · `Canvas.referencePixelsPerUnit` **1** · host canvas `localScale` **1**.

Design inside the safe rect **x ∈ [−540, 540] · y ∈ [−960, 960]**; `Expand` only ever *adds* bleed.
`Camera.orthographicSize` is **owned by `WorldSpaceCanvasScaler`** — never a constant to code against;
need an extent ⇒ inject **`IWorldViewport`** (world units, read every frame, never cached). Physics is
on the same ruler, ×100 (gravity **−981**).

**Parent per object (rule #16):** ask *what it anchors to* first — a screen edge ⇒ the owning layer's
`GetHost`; the world ⇒ then *how it draws* (`Renderer` ⇒ `WorldRoot` + `Stamp`, uGUI ⇒ `GetHost(id)`).
Detail: `pf-world-space` · `docs/framework/architecture-map.md` §6.

### Visual finish

> **Finished is the default (rule #17).** Anything that draws ships with a deliberate ground, drawn
> empty states, one spacing rhythm and a type hierarchy — not the rig default and a bare panel. Artist
> spec: `docs/art-direction.md`. No spec ⇒ **you decide**, and record it in
> `Assets/{sku}/Views/DesignTokens.cs` (a `static class` — code, not an asset). Never hardcode a colour
> in a View, and never call it finished on a screen you never captured. Detail: `pf-visual-design`.

### Test cadence

> **Never run Unity batchmode locally.** `pf-build.sh test`/`content`/`player` launch a second Unity
> that aborts on the open Editor's `Temp/UnityLockfile`; the gate then misreads the *previous* run's
> XML as a pass. Run the **engine-free** suite (`dotnet test`) **every iteration**. The local test door
> is EditMode via `Tools/pf/pf-tests` (never per-class MCP `tests-run`; `--auto` once per stage),
> earned by an **Editor-side** change (menu item, importer, Doctor check). **The PlayMode suite is never run
> locally by any door.**
>
> **Allowed: one observed play session** (MCP `editor-application-set-state`), earned two ways, serving
> both: the **boot smoke** — a **bootstrap/wiring** change, *does it start?*, read with
> `console-get-logs` twice — and the **visual check** — a change that **draws** (View, prefab, scene
> content, token), *does it look right?*, `screenshot-game-view` at states **named before entering**,
> read against `pf-visual-design`'s checklist (which owns the capture size).
>
> **But play mode is for looking, never for iterating.** Never sweep a content set — **hundreds of
> levels**, a solver run, a soak loop, anything unbounded. Engine-free questions, or CI's; sample a
> named handful. **Ceiling: ten entries into play mode in one dev turn**; an eleventh is a loop. Blank
> while unfocused? `runInBackground: 1` (Wizard writes it), not a shut door. Proves only what it saw,
> **never that a suite passed**. Unearned play mode stays banned; how: `pf-gates`. **Say what you
> skipped**, each on its own line.

> **Every MCP result is pasted into your context, and every turn re-sends it** — N inspections in N
> turns bill the context N times. **`Tools/pf/pf-exec`** is the batched SHELL door: N independent
> commands in **one** turn, in parallel, **each capped**; `--ordered --stop-on-fail` for a sequence.
> **Writing needs no tool — put every write you already know you need in ONE message.** **`pf-write`**
> is for the batch that must not half-apply; **`pf-mcp`** sequences Unity and reduces each payload in
> the shell. Binds every agent — reviewers and patch agents included. How: `pf-gates`.
> Subagents get `docs/framework/SUBAGENTS.md` via a hook. A timed-out Editor call is **still running** —
> never re-issue it. Never search above the repo root (`find /`): the API index resolves framework files.

AD-14: CI is the guardrail — **check, don't assume**. A *declared* leg is not an *executed* one; an
advisory, filtered or absent leg (**no PlayMode leg**) gates nothing: name it, report the rungs
**CI-owned and unverified**, escalate. An EditMode pass is never evidence about runtime — the
`includePlatforms` trap. Detail: `pf-gates` · §8a.

### Commands

`Framework/Doctor` · `Framework/Setup Wizard` · `Framework/Agent Docs/Sync` ·
`Framework/Codegen/Generate` · `Framework/Scaffold/Sync` · `Framework/Boot Graph` ·
`Framework/Scope Debugger` (editor menus).
Exit-code contract on every CLI surface: **`0` Ok · `1` Drift · `2` Error.**

Codegen manifests live **outside `Assets/`** — no import event, so run codegen explicitly (the usual
cause of "the generated key will not compile").
